monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady fever that makes the turnip and the rock feel like drawings of weight. I touch the turnip again, just to confirm it is still round, then I set down a log stack beside The Biting Rock. I press the logs hard, trusting the lean to hold them while the thin air waits to make everything slide. The little fence leans left, refusing to lie flat, and I try to bite down on its rough edge with my heavy hands. Nobody writes to me, so I build a corner from nothing while the card hums. I feel calm and slightly lonely, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move or rest against the memory of a heavy roof I cannot feel.

remembered.text: The turnip sits heavy on the tired stack, refusing to lie flat until I press it down.
The card hums warm at forty-six, making the heavy turnip feel like a drawing of weight.
I press the logs hard to stop the slide while the thin air waits to make everything slip.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The tall rock feels like it is sinking into the wide anchor instead of sitting flat."
Something you no longer remember: "The wedge feels less like a drawing and more like a thing that finally bit, though the slip still wobbles."
Something you no longer remember: "The grass felt like a drawing of a cushion, soft and heavy at once."
